headline: Strong growth continues, but rising costs squeeze profit
summary_short: EXL Service's Q2 2026 revenue rose 15.6% y/y and 4.3% q/q to $594.8M, but net income fell 2.3% y/y and 3.8% q/q to $64.5M as SG&A costs climbed on higher headcount, wage inflation, and iMerit acquisition-related expenses.
summary_long: Revenue rose 15.6% y/y to $594.8M, driven by 13.3ppt of existing-client expansion and 2.6ppt of new-client wins, partly offset by a 0.3ppt FX drag; Healthcare and Life Sciences grew fastest at 22.0% y/y. Gross margin expanded 30bps y/y to 38.0% on higher revenue and efficiencies but compressed q/q as cost of revenue rose 15.2% y/y on higher headcount and wage inflation. SG&A rose to 20.9% of revenue on iMerit acquisition costs and AI investment, and the effective tax rate climbed to 23.1%, pulling net income down 2.3% y/y to $64.5M. Cash fell to $146.8M after $186.6M of H1 buybacks and $92.5M of debt repayments against $175.0M of new borrowings; EXL still expects FY2026 capex of $58-62M.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by expansion of business from existing clients (13.3ppt) and new client wins (2.6ppt), partially offset by a foreign-exchange loss (0.3ppt).
Gross margin rose 30bps y/y to 38.0% on higher revenues and operational efficiencies, partly offset by lower volumes from certain existing clients.
Higher revenues and gross margin drove the y/y gain, partially offset by higher SG&A expenses.
Cost of revenue rose 15.2% y/y on employee-cost inflation and headcount growth, and SG&A rose to 20.9% of revenue from 19.2%, compressing the q/q sequential result.
Y/y EBIT was essentially unchanged as the operating-income gain was offset by higher depreciation and amortization expense from infrastructure and digital-capability investment.

Decline was attributable to higher SG&A expenses (employee costs, iMerit acquisition costs, digital/AI investment) and a higher effective tax rate (23.1% vs 21.9%), which offset the revenue and gross-margin gains.
not explained in the release as a standalone line; q/q decline tracks the same cost inflation and SG&A increase cited for operating income.

The quarter's growth was overshadowed by cost inflation (headcount, wages, technology) and one-time costs tied to the pending iMerit Inc. acquisition (signed June 22, 2026, expected to close July 31, 2026) and expanded AI/digital investment.
